item.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
item.description:
The paper presents a method that lets you decide when enough AI testing is done by giving a running upper limit on the chance of unseen failures. They built an anytime‑valid confidence sequence that can be checked after each test run and found tighter bounds than existing techniques on a real coding‑agent dataset. This helps you stop testing sooner while keeping a statistical safety margin.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for AI services, here is what to do: 1) Run your usual automated tests and record any failures. 2) Apply the algorithm to compute the upper confidence bound on unseen failures after each batch. 3) When the bound drops below your acceptable risk threshold, stop testing and deploy.

item.title: AskALCF: A Self-Improving Agentic System for Intelligent HPC User Support
item.description:
AskALCF is a self‑improving AI system that monitors and diagnoses failures in HPC user support queries, pinpointing whether the issue is missing knowledge, poor retrieval, bad prompting, model errors, or tool problems. By analysing production interactions, it reduces unexplained failures from 41.4% to 14.2% and improves expert agreement on fixes. The system offers a systematic way to keep AI support services accurate without constant manual updates.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud or HPC support, here is what to do: 1. Deploy a similar log‑analysis pipeline to track support interactions. 2. Use its failure attribution to target knowledge‑base or retrieval updates. 3. Periodically train the system with expert edits to keep accuracy high.

item.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
item.description:
This research solves the problem of huge memory costs and power use when serving large LLMs by replacing replicated HBM with an optical broadcast system that streams weights from a central server to many accelerators. They built the Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM) architecture that eliminates the need for petabytes of on‑node memory while matching or beating throughput and energy metrics of HBM systems. The result is a more scalable, energy‑efficient way to serve very large, MoE‑enabled language models across tens of thousands of GPUs.

IT Breakdown: If you manage a large GPU cluster, here is what to do: 1) evaluate if your workloads use the same large LLM weights across many nodes; 2) if yes, consider integrating an optical broadcast backbone to share weights centrally; 3) monitor memory bandwidth and power usage – a shift to OBM should reduce both significantly.

item.title: [News] Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
item.description: The article highlights a surge in AI-fueled ransomware attacks, noting a 20‑40% increase in recent months and the use of large language models to craft more convincing phishing emails and streamline negotiations. It warns that while fully autonomous ransomware is not yet common, the trend suggests rapid evolution in threat tactics.

item.title: [News] Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
item.description: Shield has upgraded its Forge platform with OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra, enabling AI agents to navigate legacy portals and automate routine support tasks that previously required human technicians. This improves response times for IT service providers handling ticketing, device, and license management systems lacking APIs.

item.title: [News] No Pilots. Few Air Traffic Controllers. What Could Go Wrong?
item.description: The U.S. FAA has introduced an AI-powered air traffic management system called SMART, which has raised concerns over potential failures after a national groundstop caused widespread flight disruptions. A pilotless Cessna flight demonstrated autonomous navigation, highlighting the rapid adoption of AI in aviation.
